summary: Unexpected SSO password-reset confirmations sent to multiple employees
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-05 08:15 and 08:47 UTC multiple Redwood employees received password-reset confirmation emails from our SSO provider despite not initiating resets. In one case a CI service account (internal-ci@redwood.com) also logged several token refresh attempts.

Impact: Potential account compromise or automated abuse of our SSO password-reset endpoint. A handful of users reported clicking the email but stopping at MFA because the prompt looked different. No confirmed account takeovers as of update. Potential business impact if service account tokens are compromised (build/deploy pipelines).

Environment: Production SSO (third-party IdP) federated with Redwood SAML; affected region: us-east. Affected users and one CI service account listed in metadata.

Observed: Password-reset confirmation emails were delivered with identical message-IDs and contained reset links to our SSO domain. Auth logs show a burst of reset-initiate API calls (~120) originating from a small set of external IPs (see logs below). Several of the reset acceptances failed with invalid_token errors; three attempts triggered our rate-limiting and returned 429. We observed unusual user-agent strings: "curl/7.68.0" and "python-requests/2.28" on the reset-initiate endpoint. The CI service account produced multiple token refresh attempts from the same foreign ASN and associated IPs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Inspect SSO provider logs for reset-initiate events filtered by timestamp 2026-03-05 08:10-08:50 UTC. 2) Cross-reference client IPs with firewall logs. 3) Attempt to trigger a reset from an external IP (blocked for test in staging only) to confirm rate-limit behavior. 4) Review CI service token refresh logs in secrets manager audit.
logs:
Auth logs (excerpt):
- 2026-03-05T08:15:12Z reset-initiate user=jordan.carter ip=203.0.113.45 ua=curl/7.68.0 id=msg-7721
- 2026-03-05T08:15:13Z reset-email-sent user=jordan.carter msg-id=msg-7721 provider_msg_id=okta-98a
- 2026-03-05T08:16:05Z reset-initiate user=maria.kim ip=203.0.113.45 ua=curl/7.68.0 id=msg-7725
- 2026-03-05T08:18:41Z token-refresh-fail account=internal-ci ip=198.51.100.22 reason=invalid_token
- 2026-03-05T08:20:03Z reset-initiate user=samir.patel ip=198.51.100.22 ua=python-requests/2.28 id=msg-7758
Firewall correlation: same IPs seen attempting SSH to unused hosts around 08:00-08:10 UTC.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed reset-initiate events were recorded by our IdP and surfaced to Redwood via webhook; payloads match our email templates.
- IPs map to two external ASNs; neither belong to our cloud providers.
- No successful password-change completions recorded for listed human users. The CI service account saw repeated refresh failures but no successful token exchange.
- Checked SSO webhook consumer: no signs of replayed webhooks in our queue; message-IDs unique.
- Reviewed recent IAM changes: none in the last 72 hours.
- Cross-referenced with #security Slack channel: similar but lower-volume events reported by one other internal team in eu-west at 07:58 UTC (possible coordinated probe).
hypothesis: Automated credential-probing or mass phishing campaign targeting our SSO reset endpoint using programmatic clients. Attackers may be attempting to trigger reset flows to harvest session links or provoke users into using supplied redirect URLs. CI token refresh failures likely collateral due to IP overlap or credential stuffing against service endpoints.
immediate_actions:
- Rotated SSO webhook signing key as precaution.
- Temporarily increased MFA enforcement for interactive logins and blocked password-reset-accept from external IP ranges flagged in logs.
- Disabled token refresh for internal-ci@redwood.com and created temporary service account key for critical pipelines.
- Notified affected users with guidance and required manual re-verification of SSO sessions.
- Opened provider support ticket with IdP and requested expedited log export for full payloads.
next_steps: 1) Complete IdP log export and provide to SRE/Sec for full correlation (owner: Luis Ortega). 2) Rotate any service credentials that showed refresh activity (owner: Infra Oncall). 3) Add stronger heuristics to block scripted UA patterns and rate-limit by IP+user for reset-initiate flow (owner: Auth Platform). 4) Run phishing simulation and targeted user outreach for affected teams (owner: Security Awareness). 5) Postmortem to Confluence and update SSO runbook with new detection rules (deadline: 2026-03-12).
comments: 2026-03-05 09:05 UTC - Luis Ortega: Confirmed activity in IdP logs. Provider has exported additional headers and raw webhook bodies; attaching link (internal) to artifacts. Marking as P1 Sev1 due to potential service-account exposure.
2026-03-05 10:20 UTC - Amelia Grant: Affected users have been paged; two acknowledged clicking link but did not complete flow. Security team to run full session revocation for those accounts.

2026-03-06 14:02 UTC - Priya Nair (Auth): Implemented temporary rule to block UA patterns and throttle reset-initiate to 2/min per IP. Observing immediate drop in reset-initiate events from flagged IPs.

2026-03-06 16:30 UTC - Luis Ortega: Provider support confirms the requests originated from a known malicious ASN; they have quarantined the outbound IPs on their side. Continuing credential rotation for the CI account.
